title: Corrected active-operation criterion for operadic localization
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads with $O$ ordinary. Assume $M_{[0]}$ and $O_{[1]}$ are spaces and $f_{[1]}:M_{[1]}\to O_{[1]}$ is an equivalence. A map over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is active when its opposite order map preserves the two endpoints. For a color $x\in M_{[1]}$, define $\operatorname{Op}_M(x)$ as follows: its objects are active maps $a:m\to x$; its morphisms are coherent commutative triangles between such maps whose source-change edge is an equivalence in $M$ lying over an identity of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Include all higher simplices of these data, and define $\operatorname{Op}_O(fx)$ in the same way. These are spaces (arity cannot change). If every induced map $\operatorname{Op}_M(x)\to\operatorname{Op}_O(fx)$ is an equivalence, then for every ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad $P$ restriction gives a natural equivalence of infinity categories
$$\operatorname{Alg}_O(P)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_M(P).$$
In particular $f$ has the universal property of an ordinary operadic replacement, at the level of mapping spaces as well as coherent algebra transformations. The hypothesis is about these fixed-arity spaces of operations, not the slice with arbitrary active source-change arrows.

source.place: Erratum Corollary E.0.1, Proposition E.0.2, and Theorem A.6.5. This explicitly uses the corrected triv,act operation spaces; the uncorrected Corollary A.6.9 is not used. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Since $f_{[1]}$ is an equivalence and $O_{[1]}$ is a space, $M_{[1]}$ is a space as well: transport inverse edges and their inverse triangles through a quasi-inverse of $f_{[1]}$. The generalized Segal equivalences in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability] identify $M_{[n]}$ with the iterated fiber product of $M_{[1]}$ over $M_{[0]}$; hence every edge in every $M_{[n]}$ is invertible, coordinate by coordinate. For $n=0$ use the given hypothesis on $M_{[0]}$. For $O$, the ordinary Segal equivalences identify $O_{[n]}$ with $O_{[1]}^n$. An edge of this product has an inverse in each coordinate because $O_{[1]}$ is a space, and the inverse triangles are coordinatewise as well. At $n=0$ the ordinary Segal condition gives $O_{[0]}\simeq *$. Thus all fibers are spaces. A triangle between active maps to a fixed target whose source-change edge is over an identity has an invertible source-change edge. Consequently the spaces $\operatorname{Op}$ in the statement coincide with the corrected triv,act operation spaces: in a triangle over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, a source-change edge lying over an inert base map between active maps must lie over an identity. Indeed its opposite is an interval inclusion; composing with the endpoint-preserving active order map forces the interval to contain both endpoints and hence to be the whole interval.

source.place: Erratum, opening correction of the triv,act slice; generalized Segal definition

proof.text: Extend the color hypothesis to an arbitrary output object $C\in M_{[k]}$. Choose its inert projections $C\to C_i$ and use their images under $f$ as the inert projections of $f(C)$. Apply [lem-coef-operadic-operation-segal-product] to $M$ and to $O$, whose zero and one fibers are spaces by step 1. Its compatibility with $f$ identifies $\operatorname{Op}_M(C)\to\operatorname{Op}_O(fC)$ with the product of the maps $\operatorname{Op}_M(C_i)\to\operatorname{Op}_O(fC_i)$. Each factor is an equivalence by the assumed color criterion, and the product of their inverses is an inverse of the product map. For $k=0$ both operation spaces are contractible by the same node, so the unique map between them is an equivalence. The statement of the product lemma retains zero-length input blocks, so operations with nullary components are included. We conclude that the operation-space comparison is an equivalence for every $C$, not merely for colors.

source.place: Proof of Erratum Corollary E.0.1, reduction from all objects to inert color projections

proof.text: Fix $C\in M_{[k]}$ and an active arrow $\alpha:X\to f(C)$ in $O$ over $[n]\to[k]$. Unpack the homotopy pullback $\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)$ of [lem-coef-operadic-active-lift-criterion]. An object is $a:D\to C$ with an equivalence $f(a)\simeq\alpha$ in the slice $O_{/f(C)}$. Projecting this equivalence to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ forces $D$ to have arity $n$ and $a$ to have the same active base map as $\alpha$, since the simplex category has only identity isomorphisms. Likewise every source-change edge of a simplex in this pullback lies over the identity of $[n]$; it is invertible because $M_{[n]}$ is a space by step 1. The equivalence in the slice is therefore precisely a path from $f(a)$ to $\alpha$ in $\operatorname{Op}_O(fC)$, with exactly the same higher compatibility data. Hence this lifting category is the homotopy fiber at $\alpha$ of $\operatorname{Op}_M(C)\to\operatorname{Op}_O(fC)$. This is the path-model homotopy fiber of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The comparison is an equivalence by step 2; replacing it by its quasi-inverse identifies this fiber with the path space ending at $\alpha$, which contracts to the constant path. Thus every $\mathcal L_f(C,\alpha)$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: Proof of Erratum Corollary E.0.1, identification of the slice fiber with the corrected operation-space fiber

proof.text: The objects $C$ and active maps $\alpha$ in step 3 were arbitrary. Apply the if direction of [lem-coef-operadic-active-lift-criterion]: its ordinary-target and inert-preservation hypotheses are exactly our hypotheses, and it requires no categorical-fibration assumption on $f$. It gives that $f$ is a weak approximation, with the meaning fixed in [def-coef-operadic-weak-approximation]. The color equivalence is already a hypothesis of the item. Therefore [lem-coef-operadic-weak-approximation-algebras] gives $f^*:\operatorname{Alg}_O(P)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_M(P)$ for every ordinary $P$, including all coherent algebra transformations. This is an application of the full categorical theorem, rather than an inference of categorical equivalence from equivalence of cores.

source.place: Erratum Proposition E.0.2 and Theorem A.6.5

proof.text: Restriction is precomposition by $f$, so its composites with postcomposition by any inert-preserving map $P\to P'$ agree with first postcomposing and then restricting, on functors, transformations, and all higher simplices. This proves the asserted naturality in $P$. Taking cores preserves the equivalence, because a quasi-inverse and both coherent inverse transformations restrict to cores. By the full-subcategory definition in [lem-coef-operadic-weak-approximation-algebras], the core of $\operatorname{Alg}_Q(P)$ has inert-preserving functors $Q\to P$ as points, coherent equivalences of these functors as paths, and all higher compatibilities. This is the space of operadic maps from $Q$ to $P$; for ordinary $Q$ it is the mapping space in the operad category of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Thus precomposition by $f$ induces equivalences of these mapping spaces for every ordinary target as well. This is exactly the universal property of the ordinary operadic replacement of $M$, now obtained together with the stronger equivalence of the entire algebra categories.

source.place: Theorem A.6.5 and Corollary A.6.6, mapping-space universal property and functoriality of restriction
